newsitem.title: UK: Colombia's $750 million 10-year bond due Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's $750 million 10-year bond due Wednesday.

text.p: Colombia was expected to launch its planned $750 million 10-year global bond on Wednesday, syndicate officials said on Monday.

They said the deal should be launched on Wednesday after the New York roadshow and priced on Thursday. The transaction would be for $750 million at a 10-year maturity and was unlikely to be increased, they said.
There was no official price talk. Traders expected a launch spread of 130-140 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury note.
Colombia's extensive roadshow for the issue ends in New York on Wednesday. J.P. Morgan and Merrill Lynch are joint lead managers for the transaction.
Last Monday, a senior finance ministry official said the issue was part of the $1.4 billion in sovereign debt the country planned to sell this year.
Colombia was last in the market in May 1996 with a $400 million five-year Eurobond at a 150 b.p. spread which has tightened by around 25 b.p.
Separately, Colombian finance minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said last Friday the country would like to launch a 30-year dollar bond this year.
Colombia is rated Baa3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB by Standard & Poor's Corp.
